- It should have an input clock signal (`clk`), a reset signal (`rst`), a start signal (`start`), and an 8-bit data input (`data_in`).

module spi_controller (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg SCK,
    output reg CS,
    output reg MOSI
);
    reg [2:0] bit_counter;
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            SCK <= 0;
            CS <= 1; // CS high when idle
            MOSI <= 0;
            bit_counter <= 0;
            shift_reg <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (start) begin
                CS <= 0; // Activate chip select
                shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data into shift register
                bit_counter <= 7; // Start with the MSB
            end else if (bit_counter < 8) begin
                SCK <= ~SCK; // Toggle SPI clock
                if (SCK) begin
                    MOSI <= shift_reg[bit_counter]; // Output the current bit
                    bit_counter <= bit_counter - 1; // Move to the next bit
                end
            end else if (bit_counter == 8) begin
                CS <= 1; // Deactivate chip select after transmission
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module for an Echo Cancellation system that takes an input signal and a reference signal to produce an output signal. The module should implement a simple adaptive filter using the Least Mean Squares (LMS) algorithm. The output signal should be the result of subtracting the filtered reference signal from the input signal. The adaptation of the filter coefficients should happen on every clock cycle based on the error signal calculated from the difference between the input and the filtered reference.
code:
module echo_cancellation (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input signed [15:0] input_signal,
    input signed [15:0] reference_signal,
    output reg signed [15:0] output_signal
);
    parameter N = 5; // number of filter taps
    parameter signed [15:0] mu = 16'h0001; // step size for LMS
    reg signed [15:0] w [0:N-1]; // filter coefficients
    reg signed [15:0] y; // filtered output
    reg signed [15:0] error; // error signal

    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                w[i] <= 16'h0000; // initialize weights to zero
            end
            output_signal <= 16'h0000;
        end else begin
            // Calculate the filter output
            y = 0;
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                y = y + (w[i] * reference_signal); // accumulate filter output
            end
            
            // Calculate the error
            error = input_signal - y;
            output_signal = error; // output is error signal
            
            // Update filter coefficients
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                w[i] = w[i] + (mu * error * reference_signal); // LMS update
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple ARQ (Automatic Repeat reQuest) system using Verilog. The system should transmit a 5-bit data word and check for an acknowledgment (ACK) from the receiver.     input clk,
    input reset,
    input [4:0] data_in,
    input ack_nack, // 1 for ACK, 0 for NACK
    output reg [4:0] data_out,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: idle, 01: sending, 10: received ACK, 11: received NACK
);

        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00;
            data_out <= 5'b00000;

            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // idle state
                    state <= 2'b01; // move to sending state
                    data_out <= data_in; // prepare data for sending

                2'b01: begin // sending state
                    if (ack_nack) begin // received ACK
                        state <= 2'b10; // move to received ACK state

                        state <= 2'b11; // move to received NACK state
                        data_out <= data_in; // resend data
                    end
                end
                2'b10: begin // received ACK state
                    state <= 2'b00; // go back to idle
                end
                2'b11: begin // received NACK state
                    state <= 2'b01; // resend data

    end

The memory pool will have a fixed size, and the allocator should keep track of allocated and free blocks. The input signals will be:

- `free_req`: Request to free a block (active high).

The output signals will be:
- `alloc_granted`: Indicates that allocation was successful (active high).
- `free_granted`: Indicates that freeing was successful (active high).
- `error`: Indicates an error (e.g., trying to free an unallocated block or allocating when no blocks are available).
code:
module memory_allocator (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire alloc_req,
    input wire free_req,
    input wire [3:0] block_id,
    output reg alloc_granted,
    output reg free_granted,
    output reg error
);
    parameter NUM_BLOCKS = 16;

    reg [NUM_BLOCKS-1:0] mem_pool; // Memory pool tracking
    reg [NUM_BLOCKS-1:0] allocated; // Allocated blocks tracker

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            mem_pool <= {NUM_BLOCKS{1'b1}}; // All blocks are free
            allocated <= {NUM_BLOCKS{1'b0}}; // No blocks allocated
            alloc_granted <= 1'b0;
            free_granted <= 1'b0;
            error <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            alloc_granted <= 1'b0;
            free_granted <= 1'b0;
            error <= 1'b0;

            // Allocation request
            if (alloc_req) begin
                if (mem_pool[block_id]) begin
                    mem_pool[block_id] <= 1'b0; // Mark block as allocated
                    allocated[block_id] <= 1'b1; // Track allocation
                    alloc_granted <= 1'b1; // Grant allocation
                end else begin
                    error <= 1'b1; // Allocation failed, block already allocated
                end
            end

            // Free request
            if (free_req) begin
                if (allocated[block_id]) begin
                    mem_pool[block_id] <= 1'b1; // Mark block as free
                    allocated[block_id] <= 1'b0; // Track free
                    free_granted <= 1'b1; // Grant free
                end else begin
                    error <= 1'b1; // Free failed, block not allocated
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple PCIe endpoint controller state machine that handles three states: IDLE, REQUEST, and ACKNOWLEDGE. The state machine should transition from IDLE to REQUEST on a 'start' signal, and from REQUEST to ACKNOWLEDGE on a 'request_done' signal. It should return to IDLE after a fixed duration in the ACKNOWLEDGE state, indicated by a 'timeout' signal.

module pcie_endpoint_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input request_done,
    input timeout,
    output reg [1:0] state // 2-bit state representation
);

    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00;
    parameter REQUEST = 2'b01;
    parameter ACKNOWLEDGE = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= REQUEST;
                    end
                end
                
                REQUEST: begin
                    if (request_done) begin
                        state <= ACKNOWLEDGE;
                    end
                end
                
                ACKNOWLEDGE: begin
                    if (timeout) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
                
                default: state <= IDLE; // Default case
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule
